hook.line: The bank clerk frowns at Rosa's old papers and goes quiet. You want to ask whether there's some problem, and you'll want to understand when she says there's no problem at all. Spanish has a some word and a no word that fit right in front of the noun.

examples.en: No, there's no problem at all.
I don't have a single document.
Do you know a good restaurant around here? (to a friend)
Some day I'm going to come back.

rule:
You already have *algo*, *alguien*, *nada* and *nadie*: something, someone, nothing, nobody. Today's words sit in front of a noun and match it.

Some, any:
*algún problema*, *alguna pregunta*
*algunos clientes*, *algunas sillas*

No, not a single:
*ningún problema*, *ninguna pregunta*

*Ningún* nearly always stays singular, even where English says any documents: *No tengo ningún documento*.

Before a masculine noun the word loses its *o*: *algún*, *ningún*. With no noun after it, the *o* comes back: *No conozco ninguno*.

After the verb, *ningún* needs a *no* in front, just like *nada*: *No hay ningún problema*. At the very start of the sentence it works alone: *Ningún banco abre los domingos*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these indefinites. The short forms *algún* and *ningún* carry an accent because they end in *n*.

options: Are there a lot of problems?
I don't have a single document.
Some day I'm going to come back.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *¿Hay ___ problema?* (*algún* or *alguno*) Is there a problem?
yourTurn.why: Before a masculine noun like *problema*, the *o* drops: *algún*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No tengo ___ pregunta.* (*ningún* or *ninguna*) I don't have any questions.
Talking about restaurants. Pick and type the whole sentence: *No conozco ___.* (*ningún* or *ninguno*) I don't know any.
yourTurn.why: No noun comes after it, so the full *ninguno* comes back.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask the clerk (polite): Do you need any document?

yourTurn.why: Some with a plural masculine noun is *algunos*.
*Algún* turns into *ningún*, and the verb gets a *no* in front.
*Ninguna* is almost always singular, so *preguntas* becomes *pregunta*.

yourTurn.prompt: Drop the *no* and start with *Ningún*: *No viene ningún cliente hoy.*
yourTurn.why: At the start of the sentence, *ningún* says no on its own.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Right before a masculine noun, *alguno* shortens to *algún*.
After the verb, *ningún* needs a *no* in front, just like *nada*.
Close. English says any documents, but Spanish keeps *ningún* and the noun singular.
*Pregunta* is feminine, so the word matches it: *alguna*.
With no noun after it, the short form isn't enough: say *ninguno*.

personal: Say two true things: a problem you have this week with *algún* or *alguna*, and something you don't have at all with *No tengo ningún* or *ninguna*.
